check_feed.description: Check that a feed address still works and see when it last published. This is the step for watching a blog, a release feed or a podcast: 'days since last post' is there to branch on, so a workflow can raise an alert when a feed goes quiet, and 'well formed' catches a feed that has just broken. An address that turns out to be a web page rather than a feed is not a failure: the step says so and lists the feeds that page links to, which is usually the address you meant. No account or API key required.
check_feed.name: check_feed

parameters.description: The address of the feed to check, e.g. 'https://arstechnica.com/feed/'. If it turns out to be a web page rather than a feed, the step says so and lists the feeds it found there instead of failing.
parameters.name: url

checked.description: The address that was checked, with the scheme filled in if you left it off.

days_since_last_post.description: How many days ago the newest item was published. This is the value to branch on to catch a blog that has gone quiet. Empty when the feed carries no dates.

export_opml.description: Turn a list of websites into an OPML file, the format every feed reader imports. Give the sites you read and get one file with their feeds in it, filed under a folder per site, ready to hand to Feedly, Inoreader, NetNewsWire or anything else. Duplicate addresses for the same feed are collapsed, and two feeds from one site that share a title are labelled with their format so they can still be told apart in a reader's sidebar. A site that cannot be reached is reported on its own and the rest are still exported. No account or API key required.

description: Find the RSS, Atom and JSON feeds a website publishes, with Feedsearch. Point it at a domain and get every feed the site has, each with its title, format, how often it posts and when it last did, so a workflow can subscribe to a blog, watch a release feed for new posts, or notice when one goes quiet. Duplicate addresses for the same feed are collapsed into one entry, and the feeds that belong to the site you asked about are not buried under the ones it merely links to. Export any set of sites as an OPML file to import into a feed reader. No account or API key required.
